kicad_symbol_note: 74xx:SN74LVC8T245 exists with the same PW pin numbers [not compared pin by pin]; safer to define the symbol from the table below

circuit.role: OE pull-up so the header is high-impedance through power-up
DIR pull-downs: default B->A = header is input
circuit.page: p21: control inputs must not float

circuit.role: series resistors on the header side [this design]
BENCH_VREF source: adjustable LDO, 0.55 V reference
LDO feedback, switched by BENCH_VSEL0 (expander pin driven low or left as input): 1.80 V
LDO feedback, switched by BENCH_VSEL1: 2.50 V; both = 3.11 V

supplies.I_one_rail_off_uA: 12 typ, 25 max on the live rail

logic: A side and DIR1/DIR2/OE referenced to VCCA; B side to VCCB. Either rail at 0 V: all outputs high-impedance (Ioff, p1). 288 k pull-downs on every data pin; external pull-ups must be <= 30 k (p21).
placement: At the bench header; ESD arrays between header and shifter, closest to the header.
notes: Two direction groups (p21 table 7-1): DIR1 sets bits 1-4, DIR2 sets bits 5-8; DIR high = A->B (brain drives the header), low = B->A; OE high = all off.

CONFLICT to settle: with BENCH0-3 in one group and BENCH4-7 in the other, UART TX on BENCH2 and RX on BENCH3 would need opposite directions inside one group. The pin table above therefore puts the EVEN lines (0,2,4,6) in group 1 and the ODD lines (1,3,5,7) in group 2: TX/clock/select on even lines, RX/MISO on odd lines.

LIMIT: this is a push-pull, direction-controlled part. Open-drain two-way lines (I2C, 1-Wire, SWDIO) cannot run through it. If the header should speak I2C or SWD, add a 2-bit auto-direction open-drain translator (TXS0102 or a second PCA9306) on two extra header pins.

VREF: 'both select lines active' gives 3.11 V, so no combination can exceed the 3.6 V limit. For a target-supplied reference the LDO must be off (BENCH_VREF_EN low) and the header then back-feeds its output: add a series Schottky or accept LDO-only.
